title: Ringed-space Tor amplitude stalk criterion and quasi-compact uniform finite bounds
statement: Let $(Z,\mathcal B)$ be a ringed space, meaning a topological space with a sheaf of commutative rings on its site of opens, and let $K^\bullet$ be an arbitrary cochain complex of $\mathcal B$-module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Work in unbounded derived categories, writing $Q$ for localization at quasi-isomorphisms [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], and compute sheaf derived-tensor vanishing using K-flat resolutions [def-trf-ringed-complex-derived-tensor-vanishing]; module derived tensors are likewise computed by K-flat resolutions [def-pc-module-kflat-complex]. For $z\in Z$, let $K^\bullet_z$ be the actual termwise module stalk complex over $\mathcal B_z$ [def-pc-module-stalk-functor]. For any integers $a\le b$, the following are equivalent: (1) $H^i(QK^\bullet\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\mathcal B}\mathcal F)=0$ for every $\mathcal B$-module sheaf $\mathcal F$ in degree zero and every $i\notin[a,b]$; (2) $H^i(Q(K^\bullet_z)\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\mathcal B_z}L)=0$ for every $z\in Z$, every $\mathcal B_z$-module $L$ in degree zero and every $i\notin[a,b]$. The ringed space need not be a scheme or locally ringed, the test sheaves need not be quasi-coherent, and no boundedness or quasi-compactness is assumed. If $Z$ is quasi-compact, meaning that every open cover of $Z$ has a finite subcover, the following are also equivalent: (3) every $z\in Z$ has an open neighbourhood $W$ and integers $a_W\le b_W$ for which condition (1), with $K^\bullet|_W$ and $\mathcal B|_W$ in place of $K^\bullet$ and $\mathcal B$, holds on $W$; (4) condition (1) holds on all of $Z$ for one pair of integers $a\le b$. No local-ring or quasi-separatedness assumption is imposed. For $Z=\varnothing$, (4) holds with $[a,b]=[0,0]$.

source.place: Tag 09U9, lemma-tor-amplitude-stalk, both implications on arbitrary ringed spaces and the finite-subcover uniform-bound consequence on a quasi-compact underlying space.

proof.text: Prepare a comparison valid for any K-flat resolution $q:P^\bullet\to K^\bullet$. Such resolutions exist by [lem-pc-kflat-resolution], applied to the site of opens of $Z$. By the kernel, image and cokernel clauses of [lem-weil-pbc-module-stalk-exact], taking stalks commutes with cohomology, so $q_z:P_z^\bullet\to K_z^\bullet$ is a quasi-isomorphism. Its image under $Q$ is invertible by [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. For any module sheaf $\mathcal F$ and integer $i$, apply [lem-pc-stalk-kflat-tensor-homology] with $A=\mathcal B_z$ and $e=\mathrm{id}$. It identifies the underlying abelian group of $(H^i(\operatorname{Tot}(P^\bullet\otimes\mathcal F[0])))_z$ with that of $H^i(Q(P_z^\bullet)\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\mathcal B_z}\mathcal F_z)$. Applying the derived tensor functor to the invertible morphism $Q(q_z)$, then $H^i$, replaces $Q(P_z^\bullet)$ here by $Q(K_z^\bullet)$. Thus the two groups vanish together. This comparison holds for every resolution, test sheaf and degree; no boundedness has entered.

source.place: Tag 09U9, lemma-tor-amplitude-stalk, proof; Tag 06YB, lemma-check-K-flat-stalks, proof

proof.text: Assume (1). Fix $z$, an arbitrary $\mathcal B_z$-module $L$, and $i\notin[a,b]$. Construct $\mathcal F=i_{z,*}L$ by [def-pc-ringed-module-skyscraper]. The degree-zero case of [lem-pc-skyscraper-complex-stalk-recovery] gives $\mathcal F_z\cong L$. By (1) and [def-trf-ringed-complex-derived-tensor-vanishing], choose a K-flat resolution $P^\bullet\to K^\bullet$ for which $H^i(\operatorname{Tot}(P^\bullet\otimes\mathcal F[0]))=0$. Its stalk is zero, so Step 1 and the isomorphism $\mathcal F_z\cong L$ give $H^i(Q(K_z^\bullet)\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\mathcal B_z}L)=0$. This proves (2) for every stalk module, without any requirement that $z$ be closed.

source.place: Tag 09U9, lemma-tor-amplitude-stalk, proof; Tag 06YB, lemma-check-K-flat-stalks, proof

proof.text: Assume (2), and choose one K-flat resolution $P^\bullet\to K^\bullet$ as in Step 1. For any module sheaf $\mathcal F$ and $i\notin[a,b]$, (2), applied at $z$ to the actual module $\mathcal F_z$, makes the right side of the Step 1 comparison zero for every $z$. Consequently every stalk of $\mathcal H=H^i(\operatorname{Tot}(P^\bullet\otimes\mathcal F[0]))$ is zero. Apply clause (5) of [lem-weil-pbc-module-stalk-exact] to $0\to\mathcal H\to0$: it is exact at $\mathcal H$ precisely when $\mathcal H=0$, and all its stalk complexes are exact. Hence $\mathcal H=0$. The chosen resolution therefore witnesses (1) under [def-trf-ringed-complex-derived-tensor-vanishing]. This proves the fixed-interval equivalence on any ringed space, including every open subspace.

source.place: Tag 09U9, lemma-tor-amplitude-stalk, proof; Tag 06YB, lemma-check-K-flat-stalks, proof

proof.text: For an open $W\subseteq Z$ and $z\in W$, identify $(\mathcal B|_W)_z$ with $\mathcal B_z$ and $(K^\bullet|_W)_z$ with $K_z^\bullet$ using the germ description of [def-pc-module-stalk-functor]. Explicitly, send a representative on an open neighbourhood $V\subseteq W$ to the same representative on $V\subseteq Z$; the inverse restricts a representative on $U\subseteq Z$ to $U\cap W$. These maps are inverse because equality of germs is equality on a smaller neighbourhood. They respect ring operations, scalar action and each differential, since all use the same restrictions. Under these identifications the module derived tensor tests in (2) are the same tests for $Z$ and $W$. The equivalence proved in Steps 2--3 therefore shows that bounds on $W$ give those bounds for every $K_z^\bullet$, $z\in W$, and that bounds for all stalks on $Z$ give the same bounds on every $W$.

source.place: Tag 0098, lemma-stalk-pullback-modules, specialized to open restriction; explicit germ argument

proof.text: Assume $Z$ is nonempty and quasi-compact and (3) holds. Choose the indicated neighbourhoods and bounds, then a finite subcover $W_1,\ldots,W_r$, with $r\geq1$. Put $a=\min_j a_{W_j}$ and $b=\max_j b_{W_j}$. For any $z$, choose $j$ with $z\in W_j$. Step 4 and the implication (1)$\Rightarrow$(2) on $W_j$ give the stalk tensor vanishing outside $[a_{W_j},b_{W_j}]$. If $i<a$ then $i<a_{W_j}$, and if $i>b$ then $i>b_{W_j}$. Thus all stalks have the common bounds $[a,b]$; moreover $a\leq a_{W_j}\leq b_{W_j}\leq b$. The implication (2)$\Rightarrow$(1) on $Z$ gives (4). This uses only a finite subcover of the neighbourhoods supplied in (3), not a claim that pointwise finite bounds automatically extend to neighbourhoods.

Conversely, if (4) holds, use $W=Z$ at every point, with its one global pair of bounds; this proves (3). If $Z=\varnothing$, condition (2) is vacuous for $[0,0]$, and Steps 2--3 imply (1) with those bounds, hence (4); (3) is vacuous as well. These arguments establish (3)$\Leftrightarrow$(4), while the fixed-interval equivalence (1)$\Leftrightarrow$(2) was proved without quasi-compactness.
